transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I know it doesn’t make sense, but the thought of going into any kind of medical office or having tests done scares me so much that I keep putting off appointments I really need. It's gotten to the point where my primary doctor suggested I talk to someone, so that's why I'm here today.

When you think about going to a medical office, are you more afraid of the procedures and the environment itself, or are you deeply worried that they will discover you have a serious, undetected illness?

It is definitely the environment and the procedures themselves that terrify me, rather than a fear of being sick. Just the physical act of walking into a clinic or the thought of lying in one of those machines makes my stomach drop. Even when I know it's just a routine check-up, the dread of being in that medical setting is what completely panics me.
How long have you been experiencing this intense fear of medical settings and procedures? Has it been going on for at least six months?

Yes, it has definitely been longer than six months. This intense fear started about thirteen months ago, right after I slipped on some ice, fractured my wrist, and had to go to the emergency room. Ever since that visit, the dread of anything medical has been a constant struggle for me.
Since that emergency room visit, do you experience distressing, unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about the injury or your time in the ER?

No, I don't have any flashbacks or nightmares about the fall or the ER visit itself. It's not that I'm reliving that day, but rather that I feel this intense dread and anxiety about any future medical appointments or going into clinics.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits an intense, irrational fear of medical settings, clinics, and procedures, which has led to significant avoidance of necessary medical care. The symptoms began 13 months ago following a wrist fracture and emergency room visit, establishing a duration of over 6 months. The fear is specifically focused on the medical environment and procedures themselves rather than a fear of having a serious illness, ruling out Illness Anxiety Disorder. Furthermore, the absence of intrusive memories, flashbacks, or nightmares rules out Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD).
